evidence.detail: rs/M is a one-method interface accepting java.util.Random and returning rs/R.
ParticleDefinition stores rs/M as the spawn-shape strategy and asks it for one generated point when a particle is created.
The matching public particle engine exposes SpawnShape with exactly Vector getPoint(Random), the same strategy role.

proposals.note: SpawnShape is a non-canonical semantic recovery name grounded in exact v308 particle behavior; public RSPS source is corroborating lineage evidence only.

evidence.detail: rs/r/c owns the characteristic particle-definition state: start/end size, start/end color, start/end velocity vectors, spawn-shape strategy, start/end alpha, lifespan, spawn rate, sprite, velocity step, color step, size step and alpha step.

Its update/derivation methods compute per-tick color, size, alpha and vector velocity changes from the configured start/end values and lifespan, while exposing the configuration to particle instances.
rs/r/a holds one rs/r/c definition and consumes its lifespan, color/size/alpha steps, velocity/gravity vectors and spawn parameters during initialization and tick updates.

A public RSPS ParticleDefinition has the same core field layout and semantics, including Vector gravity/start/end velocity, SpawnShape, alpha/size/color endpoints, lifespan/spawnRate, sprite and derived step values.

proposals.note: ParticleDefinition is a non-canonical semantic recovery name grounded in exact v308 particle behavior; public RSPS source is corroborating lineage evidence only.

evidence.detail: rs/r/a owns a ParticleDefinition reference, age counter, color, size, alpha, dead flag, position components, velocity components and depth/id metadata; construction initializes these values from the definition.

Its tick/update method increments age, marks the particle dead at definition lifespan, advances color/size/alpha, advances position by velocity, advances velocity by the definition's velocity step and applies definition gravity to position.

The matching public Particle class performs the same age/lifespan death test and per-tick color, size, position, velocity, alpha and gravity updates against ParticleDefinition; v308 stores vector components as ints directly rather than retaining Vector objects.

evidence.detail: rs/A implements rs/M, stores one rs/R point and returns a clone of that point for every Random input.
ParticleDefinition initializes its spawn-shape strategy to new rs/A(Vector.ZERO), making this the fixed-point spawn implementation.
The matching public particle engine exposes PointSpawnShape implementing SpawnShape with one stored Vector and getPoint(Random) returning point.clone().

evidence.detail: rs/R stores exactly three integer components plus a static zero instance and exposes component getters, subtraction, scalar division, in-place addition, component-scaled mixing, cloning and a three-component toString.
The rs/r particle subsystem uses rs/R for start/end velocity, gravity/velocity-step and particle position/velocity arithmetic.
A public RSPS particle engine exposes a Vector class with the same ZERO instance, x/y/z fields and subtract/divide/addLocal/mix/clone/toString surface.
